newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers urge more control on Fed policy secrets.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers urge more control on Fed policy secrets.

text.p: Two Democratic members of the U.S. House Banking Committee on Wednesday called on the Federal Reserve to implement stricter internal controls to protect the Fed's monetary policy secrets.

"The Federal Reserve's selective confidentiality requirements for its policy discussions and actions have created a dangerous inconsistency," Henry Gonzalez of Texas and Maurice Hinchey of New York said in a joint statement.
They urged Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan to implement a "strict, uniform code of confidentiality" for Federal Reserve Board and Federal Open Market Committee meetings.
Gonzalez and Hinchey said they reviewed minutes from meetings of the 12 Federal Reserve banks from 1994 to 1997, and identified the following secrecy lapses:
* Over 400 people per Federal Open Market Committee meeting may have access to "exploitable" information.
* An estimated 300 staff members and directors attend the Board of Directors' meetings of the 12 Federal Reserve Banks each month.
* 34 staff members at the Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank attended a meeting of the Board of Directors when interest rate decisions were made.

"Financial markets work best when everyone has information at the same time and a system of consistent disclosure procedures is in place," Gonzalez and Hinchey said. "Information that is secret should be strictly guarded under uniform and effective rules."
"If the Federal Reserve is going to adopt a policy of secrecy it should not be one of only selective secrecy," they said in the statement.
